materials & metallurgical engineering · cuet

Recovering value from spent materials, one reaction at a time.

I'm a materials & metallurgical engineer working on battery-material recovery, corrosion behaviour and nanostructured alloys. I turn waste streams and worn structures into data, and data into published, peer-reviewed findings.

Chattogram, Bangladesh · B.Sc. MME, CUET '25 · 6 manuscripts in pipeline
view research → get in touch
fig. 0 · subject CUET · MME · 2020–2025

I study how materials fail, and how what fails can be recovered. My thesis extracted lithium from spent batteries using an eco-friendly acid leach; my other projects span Pb-free solder alloys, rare-earth-doped battery anodes and high-entropy alloys for extreme heat.

I work across the full materials pipeline: process optimisation and kinetics, structural characterisation (XRD, XRF, SEM, TGA), and computational modelling (LAMMPS, ANSYS), then I write it up. I'm first author on a Q1 journal paper and a contributor across five more manuscripts currently under review.

Before research took over, I served as Organising Secretary of Green For Peace and Vice-President of the Chittagong Student Forum, and completed an industrial internship at BSRM's steel melting and rolling plant in Chattogram.

hands-on lab projects
project 01
Microstructure of an Al–Si piston alloy
I prepared the alloy with metallographic preparation, then used optical microscopy and image analysis to evaluate the α-Al and Si phases.
project 02
Fracture and failure analysis of metallic components
I investigated ductile, brittle, fatigue and stress-related failures with fractography and NDT techniques to identify the failure mechanisms.
project 03
Microstructure and hardness of heat-treated steel
I evaluated microstructure and Rockwell hardness after annealing, normalizing, quenching, tempering and carburizing.
04 / experience

Research experience

Undergraduate thesis
CUET, Dept. of Materials & Metallurgical Engineering
Spent lithium-ion battery recycling: salicylic acid leaching
  • Optimized acid concentration, solid/liquid ratio, temperature and leaching time for enhanced recovery of Li, Co and coexisting transition metals from spent LIB cathodes.
  • Applied shrinking-core and Arrhenius kinetic models with ANOVA to identify rate-controlling mechanisms, determine activation energies, and quantify process-parameter significance.
  • Characterized cathode materials using XRD, XRF, SEM and TGA, correlating structure and thermal behaviour with leaching performance and industrial feasibility.
hydrometallurgyxrd / xrf / sem / tgakinetics
Research project
CUET, Dept. of Materials & Metallurgical Engineering
Corrosion-fatigue behaviour of structural steel reinforcement
  • Investigated the coupled effects of mechanical stress and acidic, saline and alkaline environments on TMT 500CWR steel: mass loss, strength, ductility and unit weight.
  • Correlated quenching media, martensitic rim formation and microstructure with impact toughness and fatigue life via Charpy impact, rotating-bending fatigue, metallography and fractography.
tmt steelfatigue testingmetallography
Research project
CUET, Dept. of Materials & Metallurgical Engineering
Nano-scratch study of refractory high-entropy alloys
  • Guided and co-developed molecular dynamics nanoscratch simulations of compositionally tuned Hf–Nb–Ta–Ti–Zr alloys, evaluating friction, contact mechanics, pile-up and subsurface damage.
  • Led data interpretation and manuscript development, establishing composition- and depth-dependent relationships between elemental enrichment and deformation behaviour.

CUET, Dept. of Materials & Metallurgical Engineering
FSAE space-frame material selection
  • Conducted finite-element analysis of a Formula SAE tubular space frame using Al 6061-T6, Ti-8Al-1Mo-1V and CFRP under static, torsional and modal loading.
  • Identified torsional stiffness, not factor of safety, as the key material-selection criterion, contributing to manuscript development.

publishedQ1 · Metals and Alloysfirst author2026

Leaching kinetics and dissolution mechanism of spent lithium-ion battery cathodes in salicylic acid media

Journal of Sustainable Metallurgy · DOI 10.1007/s40831-026-01628-3

I optimized acid concentration, solid/liquid ratio, temperature and leaching time to recover lithium, cobalt and coexisting transition metals from spent cathodes. Shrinking-core and Arrhenius kinetic models, together with ANOVA, let me identify the rate-controlling mechanisms, determine activation energies and quantify how much each process parameter matters.

A companion study on process-parameter optimization is currently under review at Heliyon.
